text.aura: You give off pure sunlight. Byeong walks in and the temperature rises, in the best way. People notice you even when you're not trying, and honestly, you're often trying a little. You radiate optimism, generosity and that "let's do something fun" energy that makes a boring night instantly better. Your glow is wide and open; it touches everyone in the room. That's why you're photographed at every party and remembered by people you met once. The glow-up for you isn't getting brighter. You're already very bright. It's learning to shine with depth, so people don't just see your warmth, they feel how genuine it is. Think golden hour rather than noon: the same sun, but richer, softer and far more beautiful to look at.
text.how-people-read-you: In the first ten seconds: confident, fun, easy to approach, maybe a little loud. People assume you're an extrovert with a hundred friends, and they're not entirely wrong. They feel included around you, which is a rare gift. The misreading comes from that same brightness. Some people think you're shallow because you're so cheerful, or that you need attention because you're so visible. They don't see how much you actually care, or how hurt you get when your effort goes unnoticed. To be read more fully, let a little quiet into your presence. Listen for longer. Share one serious thought among the jokes. Your sunny aura doesn't need dimming. It just becomes more trustworthy when people see that it's real all the way through.
text.colors: Your base colors are bright Fire: red, coral, tomato, warm orange, magenta. You can wear bold color like almost nobody else, and it looks natural, not costume-like. Wood feeds Fire, so greens are a strong support: an emerald dress, an olive jacket, a green accessory against warm tones. For balance, Earth tones like camel, sand and mustard calm the sunshine into golden hour, which is gorgeous on you. Gold jewelry generally beats silver for your vibe. Be a bit careful with all-black, all-the-time. It can make your naturally warm energy look tired. If you love black, add a red lip, a colored bag or a bright shoe so the fire still has somewhere to show.
text.style: Style-wise, you're bold, warm and joyful. Statement pieces, color blocking, big earrings, a great jacket you get complimented on everywhere. Prints work for you, especially larger, confident ones. You suit outfits that move and catch light: satin, gloss, metallic thread, a little shimmer. The trap is going so loud that the outfit wears you. Pick one star per look: either the color, the print or the accessory, and let the rest support it. Hair with volume and shine fits your energy. Your best photo is in direct golden-hour light, mid-laugh, looking straight at the camera, because you have the rare quality of looking even better when you're having fun. Never let anyone talk you into "toning it down" to fit in. Just edit it.
text.vibe: The glow-up you're after is the warm host with depth. Imagine the K-drama character who's the life of every party, then one quiet episode reveals how much they've been holding together for everyone. That depth is your new layer. Try a few shifts. Spend some time listening instead of telling. Keep one plan small and intimate instead of big and public. Post fewer stories and more meaningful moments. Let one close friend see you on a cloudy day. None of this makes you less fun. It makes your fun feel safe to be around. People trust a sun that also knows how to set. You'll notice your aura reading as warmer, more grown-up and much more magnetic.
text.aura-dims: You lose your glow when you're running on empty but still performing. You keep showing up, smiling and making the jokes, but there's a flatness behind it that close friends notice. Your outfits might get louder to compensate, or you might stop caring and fall into the same tired hoodie for days. Either way, the fire is flickering. The reset is genuine joy, not performed joy. Dance in your room to embarrassing music. Spend time in actual sunlight, outdoors, without your phone. Do something creative where no one's watching, cook a ridiculous meal, paint badly, sing loudly. Say no to one social plan and don't explain. Rest isn't the opposite of shining. It's what makes tomorrow's sunrise possible.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, your aura is sunshine. Every room gets warmer when you arrive.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Coral, red, gold earrings? You were literally built for color.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One star per outfit, babe. Not five stars fighting for attention.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is golden hour. Same sun, more depth.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Let people see you cloudy once. It makes the sunshine believable.

spring.intro: Spring Wood is pure fuel for Fire, so a spring Byeong aura is the morning sun with a full tank. You come across as hopeful, friendly and full of plans, and strangers ask you for directions. You probably own a lot of yellow, coral and fresh green, and you look at home in all of it. Your challenge is overload. With strong support, your look can turn into a festival: color, pattern and accessories all shouting at once. Your glow-up is grounding. Earth, the element your Fire produces, gives camel, sand and warm brown as a base, and one bright accent does the rest. You look best as sunrise over a field: warm light on a calm horizon.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Byeong, yellow, coral and a green print at once? That's a fruit salad. Add camel.

summer.intro: A summer birthday doubles your Fire, so a summer Byeong is the noon sun, and your aura reads as loud before you even speak. People see you as confident, sociable and slightly overwhelming in the best way. Red, orange, gold and sequins come naturally, and in July you might wear them all together. Your glow-up is cooling. Doubled Fire needs Water to balance it, so bring in navy, deep sea blue and black as anchors, with one fiery piece as the star. Lighter fabrics and clean lines help your brightness feel effortless instead of effortful. The summer Byeong glow-up is not dimming the sun. It is giving the sun a sky to shine against.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Byeong, navy dress, one gold cuff. You're the sun with a proper sky behind it.

autumn.intro: In autumn your Fire is busy working on Metal, the element it controls, so a Byeong born then carries the aura of a sunset over a harvest: rich, warm, slightly tired by the end of a long day. You come across as generous and hardworking, the friend who arrived with snacks and stayed to tidy up. Your style can tilt practical because you are always doing something for someone. Your glow-up is replenishing the fire. Wood is your resource, so olive, forest green and wooden accessories feed your warmth, while amber and burnt orange let you shine. Add one gold accent that catches the light. You glow best in late-afternoon colors, the hour that flatters everyone.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Byeong, the apron energy is cute. Olive coat, amber knit, gold hoops. You're off duty.

winter.intro: Winter's Water dampens Fire, so a winter Byeong is the low December sun. Your aura reads as warm but careful, someone who brightens a room once they feel safe in it. People sometimes miss how fun you are because your winter wardrobe hides it in black and gray, the city uniform. Your glow-up is adding fuel and heat. Wood feeds your Fire, so emerald and deep green are allies, while red, coral and warm gold put the sun back in the sky. One bold colored coat against a dark street transforms how people see you on the commute. A winter Byeong in color is a lit shop window in December: people slow down to look.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Byeong, a red coat on a gray street. Watch strangers smile without knowing why.

earth.intro: A Byeong Fire born in the Earth days glows like late sun on a field: warm, generous and a little worn by the end of the day. People feel welcome around you instantly. You may notice your energy looks tired before you feel it. Fire feeds Earth, so too many sandy, beige tones can flatten you. Your glow-up is fuel. Wood feeds Fire, so bring in forest green and fresh greenery, then one bright warm accent, coral or poppy, near your face. The late-season Byeong glow is golden hour: everybody turns to look.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Byeong, green to fuel you and one coral thing near your face. Golden hour.

strength.strong: A strong Byeong Fire aura is a midsummer noon. With plenty of Fire and Wood in your chart, you radiate charisma and you dress to be seen: bright colors, big jewelry, bold patterns, sometimes all in one go. The blind spot is overpowering. Every outfit competes with the room, and the person underneath gets lost in the glare. Choose one star per look. Pair a bold color with calm navy, sand or stone, and let fabric quality do some of the talking. The sun is most beautiful when it lets the sky be blue, and your warmth reads deeper when it has space.
strength.weak: A weak Byeong Fire aura is a sun behind clouds. With little Fire or Wood support, you have a warm heart but often hide it in dull, safe clothing, and you may have decided that bright colors are 'too much' for someone like you. The blind spot is shrinking your shine so nobody can call you a show-off. Start small: a coral scarf, a red bag, gold earrings, even a yellow mug on your desk. Notice how people respond over a week. You are not too much. You are exactly the warmth the room was quietly missing.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
